analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. The only substantive change is in docs/reference/configuration.md line 685 and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md lines 314-316. Both state that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS is now forwarded to the launchd provider job, where the base text said it was not. The ssd-kv-cache.md timestamp was also bumped. Units 8d39ffcfaa638a3c:8 and :9 are surrounding context. Unit 0c2e5345ee82eaef:0 is metadata only, with no patch text to cite.

Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007, A-001). The knob is a negative-only rollback. It can disable delta checkpoints and fall back to full checkpoints. It does not widen the at-rest surface, enable the cache, or change the TTL, KEK, HMAC lookup-tag derivation or DBK3 AAD. Forwarding it into the LaunchAgent environment only lets the operator's own rollback reach installed daemons. The operator already controls that process environment (TB-003/ADV-001), and the passthrough is an allowlist, not a bypass. The documented T-041 mitigations, including the 30-minute TTL, the account-scoped salt and the KEK purge, are unaffected.

Unverified contract: the docs claim the key is now in LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys, but the Swift code (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/LaunchAgent.swift) is not in this batch. If the code is not changed to match, only documentation accuracy suffers, and the failure direction is a rollback that silently does not propagate. That is not a security regression. A reviewer of the code side should confirm that the allowlist addition is exact and does not forward other variables, such as the test-root or persistent-key controls the docs say stay unforwarded. No threat-model update is needed.
